# Professional Development for Academic Libraries

> A directory of conferences, calls for proposals, and registration deadlines for academic library and higher-education professionals, with each event checked against the organizer's own site and rated for its AI content.

Compiled by Yulia Brusova. Site: https://libprofdevelopment.vercel.app/ · Last checked: Oct 22, 2026 · 54 upcoming of 130 tracked events.

How the data is kept: each listing links to the organizer's own page. A refresh script downloads those pages, a language model extracts dates and deadlines with exact quotes, and a separate check confirms every date appears on the organizer's page before it is published. "AI focus" means: 100% AI focus = the whole event is about AI; Major AI track = the program names an AI theme or track; AI varies = a general conference included for completeness.

## Upcoming conferences


### July 2026

- [CENL Network Group AI in Libraries Webinars 2026](https://www.cenl.org/network-group-ai-in-libraries-webinars-2026/): July 10 – December 2026; Virtual; Virtual; Conference of European National Librarians; 100% AI focus. A highly specialized virtual webinar series focusing entirely on national library implementations of AI, including sovereign language models, OCR post-correction via LLMs, and automated cataloging workflows.

### October 2026

- [CLA Conference 2026 (California Library Association)](https://www.cla-conference.org/): October 22–24, 2026; Riverside, CA (Riverside Convention Center); In person; California Library Association; AI varies (general conference). Annual conference for California library professionals. Theme: 'Library Evolution.' AI ethics and technology tracks confirmed; relevant for academic and public librarians navigating AI integration.
- [EALC 2026 — 14th Eurasian Academic Libraries Conference](https://library.nu.edu.kz/ealc): October 22–23, 2026; Astana, Kazakhstan; In person; Nazarbayev University Library (Kazakhstan); AI varies (general conference). 14th Eurasian Academic Libraries Conference, hosted by Nazarbayev University Library with Kazakhstan's Ministry of Science & Higher Education. Focus on libraries' evolving roles in education, research, and society across the Eurasian region. Working languages Kazakh, Russian, and English.
- [Internet Librarian Connect 2026](https://internet-librarian.infotoday.com/2026): October 27–29, 2026; Virtual; Virtual; Information Today, Inc.; Major AI track. Leading virtual technology conference for librarians. Tagline: 'Technology, Data, and AI for Libraries.' Covers AI tools, data management, digital services, and emerging tech.
- [OpenEd 2026 — Open Education Conference](https://www.opened.org/): October 27–29, 2026; Virtual; Virtual; Open Education Association; AI varies (general conference). 23rd Open Education Conference. AI's impact on open educational resources is a primary thread — AI as threat vs. transformative tool for OER creation, adaptation, and discovery.
- [Conference on AI and Higher Education (AAC&U)](https://www.aacu.org/event/conference-on-ai-and-higher-education): October 28–30, 2026; Atlanta, GA + Online (Hilton Atlanta); Hybrid; American Association of Colleges & Universities (AAC&U); 100% AI focus; next deadline: Regular rate ends, Oct 30, 2026. Dedicated conference on AI's implications for higher education — curriculum, academic integrity, equity, faculty development, and institutional strategy. Co-located with in-person and virtual tracks.

### November 2026

- [Charleston Conference 2026](https://www.charleston-hub.com/the-charleston-conference/): November 2–6, 2026; Charleston, SC (+ virtual); Hybrid; Charleston Hub (founded by Katina Strauch); AI varies (general conference); next deadline: Regular rate ends, Oct 23, 2026. Major national conference (~2,500) on collection development, acquisitions, and scholarly publishing. Theme: "When the winds of change blow, some build walls and others build windmills." Included for professional-development completeness; AI programming varies by year.

Largest in-person gathering of educational technology researchers and practitioners. AI programming covers human-AI collaboration in learning, AI-ready curricula design, and ethical AI in instructional systems.

Operating under the theme 'Libraries Because ______,' this state association conference and trade show brings together librarians, trustees, and vendors. Included for professional-development completeness; AI programming varies by year.

Organised by the Singapore Alliance of University Libraries, the 2026 conference is themed "AI and Open Research: Building Trust, Ensuring Security, Driving Impact". It runs as a half-day pre-conference workshop followed by a full-day main conference.

Dedicated conference on responsible AI practice and governance in higher education. Institution-wide focus rather than library-specific.
- [AI and the Future of Education Conference (APUS)](https://militaryplus.apus.edu/academic-community/conferences/ai-and-the-future-of-education/): November 12–13, 2026; Virtual (free); Virtual; American Public University System (APUS); 100% AI focus. Free public virtual conference on AI in education. 2026 proposals closed August 17, 2026. Focus on practical applications, pedagogy, equity, and ethical AI use in higher education contexts.

Premier conference for digital and online learning professionals. Includes a dedicated AI Summit focused on the impact, ethics, and research behind AI in higher education — moving beyond 'how to use it.'
- [Library Journal: AI and Academic Libraries 2026](https://course.libraryjournal.com/products/ai-and-academic-libraries-conference): November 16–17, 2026; Online; Virtual; Library Journal / School Library Journal; 100% AI focus; next deadline: Regular rate ends, Nov 16, 2026. A two-day live online conference from Library Journal, held on Zoom 12:00–4:30 pm ET each day, on practical uses of AI in academic libraries. Participants earn 10 professional development credit hours and keep access to recordings for six months.
- [ALISE 2026 Annual Conference](https://alise.org/event/ALISE2026): November 16–18, 2026; Buffalo, NY, United States; In person; Association for Library and Information Science Education; AI varies (general conference). Themed 'The Good Questions,' this national conference focuses on LIS graduate education, exploring how automated systems, sensemaking algorithms, and generative AI influence information-seeking behavior and curriculum design.
- [Access Services Conference (ASC) 2026](https://www.accessservicesconference.org/conferences/2026-conference/): November 17–19, 2026; Atlanta, GA (Georgia Tech Global Learning Center + livestream); Hybrid; Access Services in Libraries, Inc. - [Core Forum 2026 (ALA Core)](https://coreforum.org/): November 18–20, 2026; Louisville, KY; In person; ALA Core: Leadership, Infrastructure, Futures; AI varies (general conference). Annual conference covering access, buildings, leadership, metadata, preservation, and technology. AI included in the technology track.
- [POD Network 51st Annual Conference 2026](https://podnetwork.org/annual-conference/baltimore-2026/): November 18–20, 2026; Baltimore, MD; Hybrid; POD Network (Professional & Organizational Development); AI varies (general conference); next deadline: Early-bird rate ends, Oct 23, 2026.
